text: @emilyhanyf @MilksandMatcha @_gongy @tyler_fong_ @shreyas4_ first picture cancled by last picture

as you know there's a curve so just depends on the cutoff you choose on low-entropy but claude gave me these numbers. top token p of 0.5 seems decent. 

i think point just stands that either we trust that the llm can model language enough to accurately calibrate token distribution or not, and i've done some basic reading but have yet to find any convincing argument on the actual harm of the watermarking here given these condition. and if the llm doesnt model {literature|writing|law|whatever} well then... yknow... bitter lesson it??

i obv care about good writing, and obv this isnt applicable to high sensitivity domains like literature, but the interesting thing about the aaronson mechanism is that the bias only applies to close-enough tournament candidates. if we trust that llms model language well, then this should genuinely kinda work and scale better the more that llms also route usecases well

quotedPost.text:
worktrees are dead. cloud agents are the future.

they've allowed me to massively orchestrate swarms of agents, all with their own computer. it's how i've been able to trust that my agents are actually doing what i want them to, because they can run their code, take videos and screenshots, and interact with UIs the same way users do.

cloud agents + pstack is the reason why i'm able to ship thousands of PRs a month with high confidence. spawn a verification /swarm of Grok 4.6 agents to "fuzz" every stack of PRs and you'll be able to let your agents merge their own work while you sleep!

although i miss writing the code myself, the combination of using @bot, @cursor_ai, and the speed, intelligence, and efficiency of Grok 4.6 makes building so much fun. the future of coding is really starting to look more like playing starcraft!
